text:
alex: heads-up — node eu-west-2a/g5-14 flapped multiple Xid(13) errors last night during batch runs. 2 jobs failed, evicted. I think it's a flaky card, but we couldn't reproduce in a short burnin. Proposing a pre-return diagnostic runbook to catch intermittent ECC/XID issues before we put these back into service. draft below.

maria: thanks — can you include a KV-cache replay step? saw reproducer when seq_len > 1024 on similar failures. also add a PCI reset attempt before claiming RMA.

tj: +1 on adding trace correlation for kernel oops and pci errors. last time we missed a pattern because logs were rotated. we should persist dmesg to s3 after each stress cycle.

infra-bot: [alert] node eu-west-2a/g5-14 reported GPU_XID_13 spike: count=4 in 2h. jobs_evicted=2. Link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/3821

alex: proposed runbook (high level):
1) Quarantine node and set `node.taint=quarantine:gpu`
2) Snapshot /var/log/nvidia and dmesg, upload to s3://redwood-gpu-diagnostics/<node>/<ts>/
3) Run 4h synthetic soak + conv microbench + kv-replay (seq_len=2048)
4) Run repeated pci reset loop (3 attempts) with 30s cooldown
5) If Xid >=3 within 4h OR ECC correctable > 100, mark as degrade and schedule RMA
6) If no repro after full cycle, 48h extended soak with telemetry sampling every 5s

Include command snippets:
```bash
# collect baseline
sudo dmesg -T > /tmp/dmesg.$(date +%s)
sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,temperature.gpu,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv -a > /tmp/gpu-state.csv
aws s3 cp /tmp/dmesg.$(date +%s) s3://redwood-gpu-diagnostics/$NODE/$(date +%s)/

# stress harness (run on node itself)
stress-ng --gpu 1 --timeout 14400s --metrics-brief || true
# KV cache replay (example harness)
./kv_replay --model resnet50 --seq-len 2048 --duration 3600 --workers 4 || true

# pci reset loop (requires root)
for i in 1 2 3; do
  sudo python3 /opt/redwood/tools/pci_reset.py --gpu 0 || true
  sleep 30
done
```

qa: can we add a lightweight fuzz input set for generation workloads? we had a failure mode with prompt lengths ~6k tokens. maybe a separate long-seq soak.

sam: i can run the first cycle on rack g5-12 tomorrow AM. will set cloudwatch alarms and persist logs to the diagnostic bucket. tagging the run with `diag-run/190123`.

kevin: what are our thresholds for immediate quarantine vs extended monitoring? the runbook above says Xid >=3 in 4h but want clarity for automation.

alex: automation thresholds proposal: immediate quarantine if any of: Xid>=3 within 4h OR single Xid correlated with ECC uncorrectable OR GPU_RESET events >1 in 1h. Otherwise extended soak: 48h + manual review. We should sync these with the oncall playbook.

maria: nit: make sure to redact job payloads when uploading to s3. replace user ids with obfuscated tokens. use /opt/redwood/tools/sanitize_logs.py

tj: i'll update the runbook doc and add a checklist: prereqs, commands, expected outputs, artifact locations. i'll push to https://docs.redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-diagnostics and notify oncall.

alex: thanks — sam let us know results by EOD tomorrow. if repro, we escalate to returns and include the full telemetry zip. :thumbsup:

sam: ack, starting at 09:00 UTC. will post a short summary here when first artifacts uploaded.
